How children learn

Four habits of a young mathematician

Every lesson follows the same four steps, so children learn how to think, not just what to write.

1

Notice the pattern

Look closely before rushing to an answer.

2

Test it with objects

Counters, coins and strips to check an idea.

3

Check your answer

Does it make sense? Try another way.

4

Explain why

Say or draw why it works. This is where learning sticks.

How it is designed

A maths enrichment program, inspired by research-based approaches used in gifted education

For curious, capable children who enjoy thinking hard about maths, whatever their starting point.

↑

Low floor, high ceiling

Every task has an easy way in and room to go further, so no child waits and no child is stuck.

?

Open investigations

Find every way, spot the pattern, make up your own puzzle, and ask "what if?".

✎

Explain and look back

Children say why it works, try a second method, and note what was hard.

★

Beyond the syllabus

We extend thinking beyond the school syllabus with depth and reasoning, not by racing ahead.

Frameworks that inspire the design include low-floor, high-ceiling tasks, Pólya's problem-solving steps and mathematical habits of mind. We do not identify or test for giftedness, we are not a GEP preparation course, and we do not promise exam or competition results.

Try one now

A taste of Lesson 1

Ages 6-8 · Frog hops
3, 6, 9, ?

A frog starts at 0 and hops 3 steps each time: 3, 6, 9 … Where does it land on its 7th hop?

In class, the answer is only half the job

Children then explain how they know: counting on a number line, adding 3 seven times, or spotting that every landing spot is in the 3 times table. Hearing three different ways is how thinking grows.

Placement

Which level is right for my child?

Levels are named by age, and each spans three ages and overlaps the next, so children can join at the level that suits how they are learning now. Start with the level that matches your child's school year:

  • Ages 6-8 (builds on Primary 1 maths)
  • Ages 7-9 (builds on Primary 2 maths)
  • Ages 8-10 (builds on Primary 3 maths)
  • Ages 9-11 (builds on Primary 4 maths)
  • Ages 10-12 (builds on Primary 5 maths)
  • Ages 11-13 (maths + coding bridge, after PSLE)

Take the free 30-minute diagnostic for the level that matches your child's school year (the Math Inquirers Placement Check for that level). Then:

  • 70% or more: enrol at that level.
  • 40-69%: enrol at that level; the tutor will note that support may help. Or choose one level down.
  • Under 40%: we recommend one level down.
  • If it was too easy (90% or more), your child may also try the diagnostic one level up.

You have the final say. You can change the level before lesson 1 at no cost, and the price is the same at every level. Ages 6-8 is the lowest level: if your child is a weaker learner there, they start with the free taster and a tutor chat.

Questions

Parents often ask

Who is it for?

Children aged 6-8 (covering P1 topics) who enjoy puzzles or finish school work easily. K2 children starting Primary 1 in 2027 are welcome after a free 15-minute readiness check, which we arrange after you register. Puzzles come in three levels, so every child is stretched.

Is it linked to MOE or the GEP?

No. Math Inquirers is an independent maths enrichment program. It is inspired by research-based approaches used in gifted education, such as low-floor, high-ceiling tasks and explaining why, but we do not identify or test for giftedness, and it is not a GEP preparation course.

Who teaches?

Lessons are planned and led by an experienced Singapore primary school maths teacher, using the Math Inquirers lesson plans, slides and workbook.

What if my child misses a lesson?

We send that lesson's workbook pages and a short catch-up guide, so your child can do it at home.

How does online work?

Live video lessons with the same group of up to 8. We post the printed workbook and kit to you before the first lesson. All your child needs is a laptop or tablet with a camera, on a table with space for the kit.

Will the price go up after Term 1?

For new families, yes: from Term 2 2027 (22 Mar) the price is S$65 a lesson. Families who join in this first intake are founding families: they keep S$50 a lesson for all of 2027, as long as they enrol in every term. If a term is skipped, the child rejoins at S$65. From January 2028 everyone pays S$65 a lesson.

How do I pay?

There is nothing to pay when you register. We confirm the group first, then send payment details. The introductory price is for families who register for this first intake.

What if we need to cancel?

You can cancel within 60 days of paying. Before the first lesson, we refund everything you have paid. After lessons start, we refund what you have paid for the lessons your child has not attended yet: for example, with 7 of 10 lessons left you get 7/10 of the fee back. If you pay in instalments, any instalment not yet due is simply cancelled. The workbook and kit are yours to keep. After 60 days, fees are not refundable. To cancel, message us on WhatsApp or email and we refund by PayNow.
